subject: Final confirmation: deploy-mode & SLOs for Velox Retail pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@veloxretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & deploy-mode tradeoffs from this morning's call

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap to lock in what we heard and recommend next steps so your engineering and procurement teams can move quickly.

Summary of your requirements (as we discussed):
- Typical production traffic: 120 qps steady-state with 10% diurnal swing (evening peak).
- Expected burst profile: short spikes up to ~300 qps for 60–90s (marketing-driven).
- SLO targets: p95 inference latency <= 120ms; tail constraints are important for your checkout flow (p99 ideally < 250ms).
- Data residency/compliance: US-only, no air-gap required; sensitive PII is redacted prior to sending.
- Integration: existing service calls Redwood via REST API; you intend to use KV caching at app layer (we discussed server-side prefix cache as an optimization).

Quick recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private):
- Hosted API: Good initial path for speed-to-market and cost efficiency if you can tolerate occasional tail spikes. We can meet p95 ~120ms for steady-state at your model size with auto-burst, but p99 tail during those 300 qps spikes will vary.
- Dedicated capacity: Recommended for predictable tail latency and consistent throughput at 300 qps bursts. Dedicated pools give reserved GPU concurrency and predictable queueing behavior — best fit if checkout latency is business-critical.
- Private VPC/on-prem: Overhead and procurement tends to push timeline 6–12 weeks. Not necessary given current compliance posture.

Open questions for you (for your engineering/prod teams):
1) How strict is the p99 < 250ms requirement? Is occasional brief breach acceptable during marketing spikes?
2) Do you want Redwood to own the burst capacity (dedicated burst) or do you prefer to start hosted with a canary and switch to dedicated before the first big campaign?
3) Who is the procurement contact to review a short pilot SOW (I can send a 1–page SOW + pricing)?

Proposed next steps:
- If you want to prioritize latency/predictability: we prepare a Dedicated pilot SOW (2–4 week pilot) + throughput benchmark plan.
- If you want to move faster: start Hosted pilot (2 weeks) with explicit guardrails and a follow-up performance gate to decide on Dedicated.

I'll attach a short SOW draft and a lightweight benchmark plan in the next email. CC'ing Marissa (ops lead) and Priyom (pricing) so they can be loaded into the thread.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0194

Attachments: none in this message (SOW to follow)

From: Alex Moreno <alex@veloxretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Li <sam.li@veloxretail.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & deploy-mode tradeoffs from this morning's call

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The p95 <= 120ms is firm for checkout flows. p99 < 250ms is a target but we need p99 breaches kept to under 5 incidents/month during campaigns.
- The 300 qps number is accurate for our expected peak bursts; those primarily last ~60–120s and happen ~2–3x/day when promos hit.
- We do redact PII client-side but user IDs and session tokens will go through Redwood.

Given that, we are leaning toward Dedicated — we prefer reserved capacity to avoid surprises during campaigns. Two asks:
1) Can you send a short pilot SOW with pricing for a 4-week Dedicated pilot (reserved pool that supports steady-state 120 qps + 300 qps bursts)?
2) We need an estimate of expected tail latency at p99 for Dedicated under your recommended configuration (model size + quantization + kv cache).

Procurement contact: Sam Li (sam.li@veloxretail.com) — please include Sam's team on the SOW. We can fast-track approvals if the pilot is scoped as a time-limited, refundable credit if we don't meet agreed gates.

On that last point, if you can outline the gate criteria (latency at p95/p99, error rate, throughput) we can expedite sign-off.

—Alex
Director of Product Engineering | Velox Retail
alex@veloxretail.com

Subject: Dedicated pilot SOW + benchmark plan (next steps & gate criteria)

Alex / Sam — attaching the 1-page SOW for a 4-week Dedicated pilot and a short throughput benchmark plan. Key points below and gate criteria at the end.

High level pilot scope:
- Reserved pool sized for 120 qps steady-state, ability to absorb 300 qps bursts for short durations (we provision headroom and autoscaling buffer).
- Model: open-vicuna-13b (quantized) with Redwood KV prefix caching enabled for hot tokens.
- Duration: 4 weeks (pilot start upon contract signature and onboarding).
- Goals: validate p95 <= 120ms for checkout flows and p99 < 250ms for at least 95% of non-chaotic traffic during bursts.

Deliverables:
- Dedicated capacity allocation + onboarding runbook (we'll set up routes and keys).
- Two synthetic bench runs (steady-state and 300 qps burst) and one production smoke test window with your staging traffic.
- Final report with latency distributions and recommendations (quantization adjustments, batching profile, cache hints).

Gate criteria (to fast-track refundable credit if unmet):
- p95 inference latency <= 120ms during steady-state (measured across 24h window post-onboarding).
- p99 inference latency < 250ms for >= 95% of sampled burst windows (we define sample windows in the benchmark plan).
- Error rate (5xx) < 0.1% sustained.

Pricing (pilot):
- 4-week Dedicated pilot fee: $18,000 (includes reserved capacity and two bench runs). If gate criteria are not met, we will refund 50% and provide 2 weeks of additional advisory at no charge.

Next actions for Velox:
1) Confirm procurement contact (Sam confirmed here).
2) Sign & return the attached 1-page SOW.
3) Book a 30-min kickoff with Marissa (ops lead) to schedule the bench runs.

Attachments included: VeloxPilot_SOW_MVP.pdf (1-page SOW), throughput-benchmark-plan.xlsx (bench details & sample workload).

I'll follow up Monday to book the kickoff. Priyom — can you please confirm the pilot pricing/discount code?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
